breakfast.name: Croissant
breakfast.description: Buttery, flaky French pastry with hundreds of delicate layers. Symbol of French baking
instructions: Make dough: Mix flour, salt, sugar, yeast, and water until shaggy
Knead 5 minutes, refrigerate 30 minutes
Pound cold butter into thin sheet
Roll dough into rectangle, place butter in center
Fold dough over butter envelope-style
Refrigerate 30 minutes
Perform 4 letter folds (turn 90°, roll, fold): refrigerate 30 min between each
After final fold, refrigerate overnight
Roll dough 1/8 inch thick, cut into triangles
Roll triangles from base to point to form crescents
Let rise 2 hours at room temperature
Brush with egg wash
Bake at 400°F for 20-25 minutes until golden
breakfast.notes: Lamination (folding butter into dough) creates the layers. Keeping butter cold is essential
breakfast.fun_fact: Despite the name, croissants originated in Austria and were brought to France by Marie Antoinette
alternatives: Store-bought puff pastry to save time
Chocolate croissant (pain au chocolat) with filling

lunch.name: Coq au Vin (Chicken in Wine)
lunch.description: Classic Burgundian dish with chicken braised in red wine with mushrooms, pearl onions, and lardons
ingredients: 1 whole chicken (4 lbs), cut into pieces
instructions: Cook pancetta in large pot until crispy, set aside
Brown chicken pieces in pancetta fat, set aside
Sauté pearl onions and mushrooms, set aside
Add garlic and tomato paste to pot, cook 2 minutes
Deglaze with red wine, scraping up browned bits
Add broth, bay leaves, thyme
Return chicken to pot with carrots
Bring to simmer, cover, braise 45 minutes
Add pearl onions and mushrooms
Braise uncovered 30 more minutes
Chicken should be tender and falling off bones
Season with salt and pepper
Garnish with parsley and pancetta
Serve with crusty bread or egg noodles
lunch.notes: The long braise develops deep flavors. Don't rush this dish
lunch.fun_fact: Coq au Vin was born out of necessity - using old roosters tough enough to require long cooking

dinner.name: Bouillabaisse (Provençal Fish Stew)
dinner.description: Luxurious Provençal seafood stew from Marseille with saffron, fennel, and orange. Served with rouille and crusty bread
ingredients: 2 lbs mixed white fish (sea bass, halibut, monkfish)
instructions: Heat oil in large pot over medium heat
Sauté fennel and onion until soft
Add garlic and cook 1 minute
Add tomatoes and wine, simmer 5 minutes
Add broth, bay leaf, thyme, orange zest
Simmer 20 minutes to develop flavors
Steep saffron in 1/4 cup warm broth, add to pot
Increase heat to medium-high
Add firm fish pieces first
Simmer 5 minutes
Add mussels and shrimp
Cook 5-8 minutes until shellfish opens and fish is cooked
Season with salt and pepper
Serve in wide bowls with broth, crusty bread, and generous rouille
dinner.notes: Use highest quality fish and shellfish. Authentic bouillabaisse uses specific Mediterranean fish
dinner.fun_fact: Bouillabaisse is protected by an official recipe and charter in Marseille, France

snacks.name: Macarons (Almond Meringue Cookies)
snacks.description: Delicate French almond cookies with smooth dome shape, filled with ganache or buttercream
instructions: Sift powdered sugar and almond flour together 3 times
Beat egg whites until soft peaks form
Gradually add granulated sugar while beating
Continue beating until stiff, glossy peaks form
Add vanilla and food coloring
Gently fold dry ingredients into meringue in 3 additions
Pipe 1-inch discs onto parchment paper using piping bag
Let sit at room temperature 30 minutes (shells form)
Bake at 300°F for 15-18 minutes (bottoms should be set)
Cool completely on baking sheet
Pipe filling (ganache or buttercream) on flat side of half
Sandwich with another macaron
Let set 24 hours for best texture
snacks.notes: Macarons are temperamental - humidity affects success. Precise measurements critical
snacks.fun_fact: Macarons originated in Italy but became famous in France, especially Paris where Ladurée and Pierre Hermé are legendary
alternatives: Store-bought almond flour to save time
Pre-made filling instead of homemade ganache

desserts.name: Crème Brûlée (Burnt Cream)
desserts.description: Silky vanilla custard with caramelized sugar topping. Iconic French dessert
instructions: Heat cream with vanilla bean (scrape seeds into cream) until steaming
Let steep 30 minutes
Whisk egg yolks with 1/4 cup sugar until pale
Slowly temper yolks by adding warm cream while whisking
Strain through fine mesh
Add salt
Pour into ramekins
Place ramekins in water bath (hot water halfway up sides)
Bake at 325°F for 30-40 minutes (centers should jiggle slightly)
Cool completely, then refrigerate at least 4 hours
Just before serving, sprinkle remaining sugar on top of each
Use torch to caramelize sugar until deep amber
Let cool 1 minute before serving (sugar hardens to crack)
desserts.notes: Water bath is essential for creamy texture. Don't overbake
desserts.fun_fact: Crème Brûlée became trendy globally in the 1980s-90s due to its elegant presentation and simple preparation
alternatives: Skip torch and use oven broiler
Add liqueur to custard for different flavor

nonAlcoholicDrinks.name: Café au Lait (Coffee with Milk)
nonAlcoholicDrinks.description: Strong coffee mixed with hot milk in equal proportions. Traditional French breakfast drink
instructions: Brew strong coffee (darker roast preferred)
Heat milk until steaming
Pour coffee into large bowl or cup
Pour hot milk into coffee simultaneously
Mix well
Add sugar if desired
Drink from bowl using bread to dip (traditional)
nonAlcoholicDrinks.notes: The ratio of coffee to milk is crucial - true café au lait is 50/50
nonAlcoholicDrinks.fun_fact: French breakfast culture revolves around café au lait and croissants

alcoholicDrinks.name: Bordeaux Wine
alcoholicDrinks.description: Premium red wine from Bordeaux region, typically blend of Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot
instructions: Serve at room temperature (16-18°C)
Open 30 minutes before serving to let breathe
Pour into wine glass
Appreciate color and aroma
Sip slowly, noting tannins and fruit notes
alcoholicDrinks.notes: Quality Bordeaux improves with age and can be cellared for decades
alcoholicDrinks.fun_fact: Bordeaux wines are among the world's most prestigious and expensive wines
